newsitem.title: MEXICO: Inbursa sold big stake in UMS 2007 global.
newsitem.headline: Inbursa sold big stake in UMS 2007 global.

text.p: Mexican bank Grupo Financiero Inbursa was a major holder of the 2007 Mexico global bond that was increased in amount by $500 million on Tuesday, but has sold much of its stake, bank sources said.

The banking group, owned by billionaire Carlos Slim who is considered Mexico's most savvy trading brain, "had a (large) position, but currently it has a small position," a source at the bank told Reuters.
In a statement on Tuesday, the Finance Ministry said it raised the amount of the 10-year global issue by $500 million from $1 billion "because of strong demand from foreign investors".

Market sources in New York and Mexico said Slim's Inbursa was rumored to have bought a major chunk of the issue and then to have sold -- possibly at a big profit -- before the Mexican government raised the amount.
The Inbursa source declined to comment on this speculation. Finance Ministry officials also declined comment.
